answer: We formalize a consensus protocol where each node must lock a dynamic opportunity-cost bond B_i on an isolated network island. When an adversarial validator attempts to mirror multiple virtual identities to dominate rewards, a subgame-perfect slashing matrix activated by zero-knowledge verifiable delay proofs executes, depleting the attacker's staked collateral. This capital barrier transforms the payoff function into a negative expectation, rendering the honest Nash equilibrium a stable oasis. Thus, identity multiplication yields negative utility.
